tool.name: rMATS
tool.description: detect differential alternative splicing between two groups of RNA-seq BAMs

regex.description: The PAIRADISE paired statistical model failed

tool.command: #set $g1 = [] #for $bam in $group1: #if $bam: #silent $g1.append(str($bam)) #end if #end for #set $g2 = [] #for $bam in $group2: #if $bam: #silent $g2.append(str($bam)) #end if #end for ## with one group rmats runs no test at all, so the paired checks only apply to two groups #if str($stats.model) == 'paired' and $g2 and len($g1) != len($g2): >&2 echo 'The paired statistical model needs the same number of BAM files in both groups, listed in matching order.' && exit 1 && #end if mkdir -p out tmp && ## rmats reads the annotation as plain text and crashes on a gzipped one #if $gtf.is_of_type('gtf.gz'): gunzip -c '$gtf' > annotation.gtf && #end if printf '%s\n' '${",".join($g1)}' > b1.txt && #if $g2: printf '%s\n' '${",".join($g2)}' > b2.txt && #end if rmats.py --b1 b1.txt #if $g2: --b2 b2.txt #end if #if $gtf.is_of_type('gtf.gz'): --gtf annotation.gtf #else: --gtf '$gtf' #end if -t '$t' --readLength $readLength $variable_read_length --libType '$libType' $allow_clipping --nthread \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1} #if str($stats.model) == 'unpaired': --cstat $stats.cstat #elif str($stats.model) == 'paired': #if $g2: --paired-stats #end if #else: --statoff #end if #if str($novel.novelSS) == 'yes': --novelSS --mil $novel.mil --mel $novel.mel #end if --task both --od out --tmp tmp && ## rmats ignores the exit status of its statistics helpers, so a helper killed mid-write leaves ## a short table and a green job; every counted event must reach the final table for counts in JC JCEC; do for event in SE A5SS A3SS MXE RI; do n_counted=\$(awk 'END { print NR - 1 }' "out/\$counts.raw.input.\$event.txt") || exit 1; n_reported=\$(awk 'END { print NR - 1 }' "out/\$event.MATS.\$counts.txt") || exit 1; if [ "\$n_counted" -ne "\$n_reported" ]; then >&2 echo "rMATS counted \$n_counted \$event events (\$counts) but reported \$n_reported: a statistics step failed"; exit 1; fi; done; done

param.name: group1
param.label: BAM files for sample group 1 (--b1)
param.help: Replicates of the first condition (the treatment in nf-core/rnasplice), reported as SAMPLE_1. For the paired model use a list collection, so that the replicate order is under your control.

param.name: group2
param.label: BAM files for sample group 2 (--b2)
param.help: Replicates of the second condition (the control in nf-core/rnasplice), reported as SAMPLE_2. Leave empty to count events for group 1 alone; no differential test is run then, whichever model is chosen below.

param.name: gtf
param.label: Gene annotation (GTF)
param.help: Must use the same chromosome names as the BAM files

param.label: Read length
param.help: Set this to the read length of your data. It is used to normalise the inclusion and skipping isoform lengths (IncFormLen, SkipFormLen). nf-core/rnasplice uses 40 unless told otherwise.

param.label: Allow reads whose length differs from the read length
param.help: Without this, rMATS discards every read that is not exactly the read length above, e.g. after adapter or quality trimming

param.label: Library strandedness
param.option: Reverse stranded, read 1 antisense to the transcript (fr-firststrand, e.g. dUTP, Illumina TruSeq Stranded)
Forward stranded, read 1 sense to the transcript (fr-secondstrand, e.g. Ligation, Standard SOLiD)

param.label: Use soft- or hard-clipped alignments
param.help: rMATS skips clipped alignments by default. nf-core/rnasplice turns this on, which matters for STAR alignments with soft-clipping.

param.label: Splicing difference cutoff
param.help: Null hypothesis cutoff for the difference in inclusion level between the groups. The default 0.0001 tests for any difference above 0.01%.

param.label: Minimum intron length
param.help: Only used for novel splice site detection

param.label: Maximum exon length
param.help: Only used for novel splice site detection

collection.name: jcec_tables
collection.label: ${tool.name} on ${on_string}: events, junction and exon counts (JCEC)

has_text.text: needs the same number of BAM files in both groups

tool.help:
## What it does
rMATS (here rMATS-turbo) detects alternative splicing events from RNA-seq alignments and tests whether their inclusion levels differ between two groups of samples. It reports five event types:
- **SE**: skipped (cassette) exon - **A5SS** / **A3SS**: alternative 5' or 3' splice site - **MXE**: mutually exclusive exons - **RI**: retained intron
This wrapper runs the BAM-input mode in a single step (`--task both`), the way nf-core/rnasplice does.
## Use restrictions
rMATS-turbo is not under an OSI-approved license. Its license makes the software available to academic and non-profit institutions for research purposes, under the terms of the 2-Clause BSD License. For use by, or transfer to, commercial entities it asks you to contact the authors first. Read the [rMATS-turbo LICENSE](https://github.com/Xinglab/rmats-turbo/blob/v4.4.0/LICENSE) before using this tool.
## Inputs
- Two groups of coordinate-sorted BAM files, one per replicate, e.g. STAR alignments. Group 1 is reported as `SAMPLE_1` and group 2 as `SAMPLE_2`. Within a group the per-replicate values are comma-separated in input order: the element order of a collection, or Galaxy's own order (not the click order) when several history datasets are selected. Use list collections when the order matters, as it does for the paired model. - A GTF annotation, plain or gzipped, that matches the reference the reads were aligned to.
Leave group 2 empty to count events in one group only. The tables then have empty group 2 columns and `NA` p-values, whichever statistical model is selected.
## Choosing parameters
- **Read length**: the read length of the data. With *Allow reads whose length differs from the read length* switched on (the default here and in nf-core/rnasplice) trimmed reads are kept, and the value only sets the effective isoform lengths used to normalise inclusion levels. - **Library strandedness**: getting this wrong for a stranded library discards most reads. - **Statistical model**: the default is rMATS' own test for unpaired replicates. The paired model (PAIRADISE) is for designs where replicate *i* of group 1 and replicate *i* of group 2 come from the same individual. It needs the same number of BAM files in each group, in matching order, so supply both groups as list collections whose elements line up. nf-core/rnasplice turns the paired model on by default.
## Outputs
- **Summary**: per event type, the number of events found and the number significant at FDR <= 0.05, for junction counts and for junction plus exon counts. - **Events, junction counts (JC)**: a list with one table per event type, counting only reads that span a splice junction. - **Events, junction and exon counts (JCEC)**: the same events counted with reads on the alternative exon body as well.
Main columns of each event table:
| Column | Meaning | | --- | --- | | `IJC_SAMPLE_1`, `SJC_SAMPLE_1`, `IJC_SAMPLE_2`, `SJC_SAMPLE_2` | Inclusion and skipping read counts per replicate | | `IncFormLen`, `SkipFormLen` | Effective lengths of the inclusion and skipping forms | | `PValue`, `FDR` | Significance of the difference between the groups | | `IncLevel1`, `IncLevel2` | Inclusion level (PSI) per replicate | | `IncLevelDifference` | Mean inclusion level of group 1 minus that of group 2 |
Coordinates are 0-based for starts and 1-based for ends, as in the column names.
